transcript.text: Every so often when I put the washing machine on the whole kitchen power goes off and I have to go to the fuse box and flick the switch back up. It doesn't happen every time. Indesit, IWE 7 something.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. An intermittent trip like this is an electrical fault, not normal behaviour. The most common cause is the heater element leaking electricity to earth once the machine starts heating, often a few minutes into a wash. If it trips immediately, the more likely area is the plug/lead, mains filter or internal wiring; if it happens on draining or spin, the pump or motor circuit moves up the list. 1. Look over the plug and visible mains lead for scorching, cracking, crushed sections or looseness. Any damage means leave it disconnected for an engineer.
2. Check for water on the floor or beneath the machine. Water reaching wiring can also cause an intermittent trip; do not move or open the machine to investigate internally. The useful clue is the timing of the trip on earlier washes: immediately, filling, a few minutes into washing, or on drain/spin? That will tell the engineer which circuit is most suspect.

Thanks. I've been keeping notes: over the last month it has tripped roughly 1 in 4 washes, always a few minutes into a 40 or 60 degree wash. It has never tripped on a cold wash, a quick 30, or rinse and spin. The plug looks fine, isn't warm and has no marks, and the floor around the machine is dry. I haven't looked inside it. I have been resetting the switch each time, and I haven't smelled burning or seen any sparks.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. That timing is a very strong match for the heater element leaking current to earth as it starts heating. A 40°C or 60°C wash reaches the heating stage a few minutes after filling; cold, 30°C/quick and rinse-and-spin programmes may not use the heater in the same way. Do not use the machine again or reset the breaker to run further tests. It needs a qualified appliance engineer or electrician to test the heater’s insulation to earth, with the appliance isolated. If that test suggests leakage, the heater element is the likely failed component; they should also inspect its terminals and wiring for heat or water damage. A control-board fault is possible but much less likely from this pattern. This is usually a repairable fault, but the engineer will need the full model number from the rating label to ensure the correct part is identified.

Mains lead, plug, mains filter or internal wiring fault (medium)
Drain pump or motor electrical fault (low)

Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that.
